input: height is an array of n nonnegative safe integers representing unit-width bars. Let H be the maximum height, or zero when empty; mathematical n * H must be at most 9007199254740991. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. JavaScript integers are primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Nonnegative integer total water retained above the bars, equal to the sum over i of min(max(height[:i+1]), max(height[i:])) - height[i]. Empty input returns zero.
mutation_aliasing: Input height and all caller aliases remain unchanged. Only scalar working state is retained during the call; the Solution object retains no state.
numeric: All maxima, differences and accumulated water are exact safe integers under n * H <= 9007199254740991. Each iteration settles the side with the smaller established boundary; the newly seen current bar can only raise that side boundary. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
